about: What if your password were 20 letters long. Factory #23, backlog row 27 (whatif-password), playlist How tech works. Packaging 5/6. One hard idea: every extra random lowercase letter multiplies the possible passwords by 26, so 8 random letters fall in about two weeks and 20 would take over four quadrillion years (our math) on Hive Systems' 2026 rig, but a reused or dictionary-word password falls instantly at any length, which is why two-step login still matters. Sources, all read 2026-11-06: Hive Systems, 'Are Your Passwords in the Green?' (2026 Password Table, published July 14, 2026, modified July 21, 2026), hivesystems.com/password: table header 'Hardware: 16 x RTX 5090 | Password hash: bcrypt (10)'; 'two 8x RTX 5090 setups running at a measured 138,675 hashes per second combined'; Lowercase Letters column: 8 = 2 weeks, 9 = 1 year, 12 = 21k years, 18 = 6tn years (the table ends at 18); 'These metrics assume passwords are randomly generated.'; 'Password table if your password has been previously stolen, uses dictionary words, or if you reuse it between websites.' every cell 'Instantly'; FAQ 'Each additional character multiplies the number of possible combinations far more than adding another symbol type does'. Our math: 26^20 / 138,675 per s = 4.55 quadrillion years (checked against the table: 26^8 -> 17.4 days, 26^12 -> 21,806 years, 26^18 -> 6.7 trillion years). NIST SP 800-63B-4 (July 2025): 'Verifiers and CSPs SHALL require passwords that are used as a single-factor authentication mechanism to be a minimum of 15 characters in length.' CISA, Multifactor Authentication topic page (undated): 'even if you have a complex password, bad cyber actors unfortunately still have ways of getting past it.' Defensive only: no tools, wordlists or methods. No AI tag anywhere (Isac, 2026-11-03). dur is the chain estimate; Ming reads about 0.855x, so expect about 31-32 s.
